html.h1: Pie, Donut and Nightingale Rose Charts
html.p: All three chart types use a single pie series. The key differentiator is the radius property:
For pie-type charts, data is embedded directly in the series.data array as {name: 'Label', value: 100} objects. No seriesDataIndexBinding or xAxisDataIndexBinding is required when using static data.

Each slice is defined by a name and a value. ECharts automatically calculates and displays percentages. Setting tooltip.formatter to '{b}: {c} ({d}%)' shows the category name, raw count, and computed percentage in the hover tooltip.
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Log Sources by Volume',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    trigger: 'item',
    formatter: '{b}: {c} events ({d}%)'
  },
  legend: {
    orient: 'vertical',
    left: 'left',
    top: 'middle'
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Log Source',
      type: 'pie',
      radius: '55%',
      center: ['60%', '55%'],
      data: [
        { value: 42350, name: 'Web Application' },
        { value: 28100, name: 'Firewall' },
        { value: 19800, name: 'Database' },
        { value: 15400, name: 'Authentication' },
        { value: 9600,  name: 'Network IDS' },
        { value: 4750,  name: 'Endpoint' }
      ],
      emphasis: {
        itemStyle: {
          shadowBlur: 10,
          shadowOffsetX: 0,
          shadowColor: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.5)'
        }
      }
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">380</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: Setting radius to a two-element array creates an inner hole. Combine with itemStyle: { borderRadius: 8 } for rounded arc ends and a polished look. The label can be hidden normally and revealed on hover via emphasis.label.
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Traffic by Source',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    trigger: 'item',
    formatter: '{b}: {c} ({d}%)'
  },
  legend: {
    top: '5%',
    left: 'center'
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Traffic Source',
      type: 'pie',
      radius: ['40%', '70%'],
      avoidLabelOverlap: false,
      itemStyle: {
        borderRadius: 8,
        borderColor: '#fff',
        borderWidth: 2
      },
      label: {
        show: false,
        position: 'center'
      },
      emphasis: {
        label: {
          show: true,
          fontSize: 16,
          fontWeight: 'bold'
        }
      },
      labelLine: {
        show: false
      },
      data: [
        { value: 1048, name: 'Search Engine' },
        { value: 735,  name: 'Direct' },
        { value: 580,  name: 'Email Campaign' },
        { value: 484,  name: 'Social Media' },
        { value: 300,  name: 'Other' }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">380</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: Adding roseType: 'area' makes each sector's radius proportional to its value, which amplifies visual differences between categories. The two-element radius sets the minimum and maximum physical radius in pixels, preventing very small values from becoming invisible.
This chart type works well for cyclic or ranked data such as monthly counts, alert severity distributions, or top-N categories.

pre.code: series: [{ type: 'pie', radius: [20, 130], roseType: 'area', itemStyle: { borderRadius: 7 }, data: [ { value: 380, name: 'Jan' }, { value: 820, name: 'Jul' }, ... ] }]
